articleTitle: Hand Gesture Classification for Individuals with Disabilities Using the DenseNet121 Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The sign language functions as a method of communication for people who are deaf and mute, utilizing recognized signs or bodily gestures to convey meanings. It incorporates shapes, hand movements, directions, and facial expressions. A single sign not only represents a word but also communicates a particular tone. For many deaf individuals, verbal communication is not an option, and they may also face challenges in reading and writing. Consequently, the development of a sign language translation system, or more precisely, a sign language recognition (SLR) system, holds significant importance in their lives. SLR is highly sought after due to its potential to facilitate communication between those who are deaf and those who hearing individuals. This field represents a crucial area of research within the realm of human-computer interaction studies. To tackle this issue, we employed the DenseNet121 Model. Our approach involved using the DenseNet121 Model alongside a dataset representing the ASL Alphabet, encompassing 24 classes corresponding to English sign language letters (excluding the letters J and Z, which involve movement). The training dataset comprised 27,455 instances, while the test dataset consisted of 7,172 instances. During the training process, we allocated Using 80% of the dataset for training and setting aside the remaining 20% for testing. The outcomes of our proposed model were exceptionally encouraging, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 97% and 96% validation accuracy. This success underscores the potential effectiveness of our model in automatically recognizing American Sign Language gestures, thereby enhancing facilitating communication and access for people who are hearing-impaired.

articleTitle: SOC Estimation Using Extended Kalman Filter in Electric Vehicle Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This paper delves into the pivotal role of State of Charge (SOC) estimation in electric vehicle (EV) battery management, employing the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) to enhance accuracy and reliability using Custom Neural Network(NNET) using MATLAB. Amidst growing environmental concerns and the shift towards renewable energy sources, lithium-ion batteries emerge as essential for their high energy density and longevity. However, precise SOC estimation remains a challenge, influencing both vehicle performance and battery lifespan. Traditional methods like Coulomb counting and voltage-based estimation fall short in dynamic conditions. The EKF, known for its adeptness in handling non-linear systems, offers a promising solution. By comparing predicted and measured voltages, the EKF adjusts internal states, refining SOC estimations. This research presents a comprehensive implementation and evaluation of the EKF in SOC estimation, showcasing its superiority over conventional methods through simulation results through MATLAB using real time data.The real SOC and estimated SOC is compared with ANN for error correction.The findings not only underscore the EKF’s potential in improving battery management systems but also highlight its adaptability to real-world conditions, marking a significant step towards efficient and sustainable EV technologies.

articleTitle: Advancing Power Conversion: A Comprehensive Survey on Reduced Multilevel Inverters, Switching Techniques, And Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Cascaded Multilevel Inverters (CMIs) have become apparent as promising remedies for applications requiring a great deal of power, offering advantages like lower harmonic distortion, higher power handling capacities, and better voltage quality. This survey explores the diverse landscape of switching techniques and controllers employed in cascaded multilevel inverters, aiming to offer a thorough summary of the most recent advancements. First, the survey classifies the different switching methods used in CMIs, for example Space Vector Modulation (SVM), Pulse Width Modulation (PWM), and Selective Harmonic Elimination (SHE). Each technique is examined in terms of its impact on inverter performance, efficiency, and harmonic content in the output waveform. Special attention is given to recent advancements in hybrid and adaptive switching strategies, offering insights into the potential for enhancing inverter operation under varying load conditions. Next, the survey explores the wide variety of controllers used in CMIs, including both closed-loop and open- loop control approaches. Open-loop control strategies, like carrier-based modulation, are analyzed for their simplicity and effectiveness in basic applications. In contrast, closed-loop control strategies, such as Model Predictive Control (MPC) and Proportional-Integral (PI) control, are explored for their ability to regulate output voltage and current precisely, even in dynamic and unpredictable environments. Furthermore, the survey delves into the integration of intelligent control algorithms, like artificial neural networks and fuzzy logic, highlighting their potential in optimizing CMIs for specific applications. The impact of controllers on overall system stability, efficiency, and response time is thoroughly examined.

articleTitle: Analysis of modified Buck-Boost Converter in Battery charging system by using solar energy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: One type of non-isolated DC-DC converter which can transit between buck, boost and buck -boost modes is the conventional buck-boost converter which consists of two switches. The gate triggering signals allow the circuit topology to alter the modes of circuit operation. A novel redesigned structure of the Two-Switch buck-boost topology is presented in this work. The suggested converter contains only less conduction loss and switching MOSFETs than a traditional Two-Switch buck-boost converter even if it has the same total number of components. As a result, there is less power loss and so the efficiency is enhanced in the restructured converter. Additionally, the MOSFETS source terminals in the proposed topology are directly linked to the ground. Hence, the low-side gate driver integrated circuit is easily adopted to trigger the MOSFETs and because of it the circuit complexity is reduced. As solar energy is stochastic in nature, the DC-DC converters become vital part of the battery storage systems. The modified circuit is designed for the input voltage of 24 V suitable for battery storage system by using solar energy and the simulation is carried out using MATLAB/SIMULINK to verify the efficiency enhancement of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: ReLU Activated Attention UNet Encipher Decipher Framework based Species Classification of Butterfly
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The recognition and categorization of butterflies is crucial for the preservation of butterfly species in the fields of entomology, computer vision and deep learning. Environmentalists have long utilized butterflies as model organisms in the research on the effects of habitat degradation, dispersion, and warming temperatures. This paper recommends Relu Activated Attention UNet (RAA-UNet) that categorizes the nine butterfly species with high precision. The Butterfly Dataset contains 1664 butterfly images that were used in this investigation. The dataset consists of 832 photos of butterflies and 832 related images that have been segmented. The proposed RAA-UNet starts by creating masked butterfly pictures by masking the original image with a segmented butterfly image. To classify the butterfly species, the masked butterfly pictures are assigned to Attention UNet with Decoder and Encoder combined with the Attention gate and activated using Relu Activation function. The proposed RAA-UNet and conventional CNN models are fitted to the masked butterfly pictures. As demonstrated by the experiments, the RAA-UNet model works better with a high accuracy of 97.75% in the classification of butterfly species.

articleTitle: Facial Recognition System for Law Enforcement: An Integrated Approach Using Haar Cascade Classifier and LBPH Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Face recognition is an area of computer vision and image processing that is quickly expanding, with many uses in security, surveillance, and biometric identity. The proposed model is to develop a criminal identification system based on face recognition using OpenCV, Haar cascade classifier, LBPH, and AdaBoost algorithm. The problem that this project aims to address is the identification and tracking of criminals, which is a crucial duty for law enforcement organisations. The suggested technology is capable of real-time facial recognition and detection of criminals, which is achieved through the use of face recognition and facial detection methods based on machine learning. The system can register criminals and manage their data through a dataset, enabling the tracking and identification of criminals through CCTV footage or manually provided images. Compared to existing technologies, the proposed system is faster, more accurate, robust, reliable, and easy to use. The usage of machine learning-based methods for identifying and recognising faces enables a more accurate and efficient criminal identification system, which is critical in today's world.

articleTitle: IoT Based Air Quality Monitoring System for Apartment Building
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: India has been undergoing rapid urbanization. The indoor safety of residents, particularly in densely populated areas, is of paramount concern. The pervaded use of liquefied petroleum gas for domestic requirement, together with the challenges of voguish urban living, augments the urgency to address potential hazards that results from gas leakage. These covers fire outbreaks, explosions, and health implications. This paper focuses on the design and development of an innovative IoT-enabled safety assurance system against gas leakages in an apartment building. The system is designed to revolutionize safety protocols within indoor spaces. The system incorporates IoT enabled gas sensors, that serve as the client, placed in each apartment, a cloud server, a notification unit, and a graphical user interface. The proposed system monitors, notifies and records the air quality of all apartments in the building. The system combines state-of-the-art hardware setup and cloud-based infrastructure for real time detection of gas leakage. The suggested system is tested for its performance under different conditions. The proposed system is expected to be a proactive approach to prevent incidents related to gas leakage, minimizing health risks and property damage.

articleTitle: IMU Data Based HAR Using Hybrid Model of CNN & Stacked LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) keeps the track of various activities in different domains including health, security, sports and robotics. Inertial sensors – specifically, gyroscopes and accelerometers – can be used for these purposes and can now also be found in the accelerometer chip or inertial measurement unit of common smartphones and smartwatches. The widespread use of these smart devices necessitates the acquisition of activity data for HAR systems. Unlike previous studies, we propose the hybrid model of CNN & Stacked-LSTM which is an integration of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and long-short term memory networks (LSTMs) to complete the task. Behind our design, lies the idea that the integrating architecture is capable of capturing the spatial features as well as temporal features of sequential data which are equally important for the prediction of the future values. We evaluate the model in benchmark dataset UCI-HAR to demonstrate its comparative performance with the existing work. Our proposed model achieves an accuracy of 93.4%, displaying its effectiveness. We trust that the architecture can be used in various social sectors attached with HAR.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control of PSS and SSSC Using Ant Colony Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Small signal stability refers to the power system’s ability to maintain synchronism when subjected to minor disturbances. Instabilities that may occur in two main forms: a slow increase in rotor angle due to not enough synchronizing torque, and rotor oscillations with increasing size due to not enough damping torque. To solve these problems, generators are equipped with PSSs, which improve the damping of low-frequency oscillations, usually between 0.2 to 3.0 Hz, making the power system more stable. Simultaneously, the SSSC as damping controller, also can contributes to power flow control and voltage stability by dynamically regulating line impedance. However, a proper coordination between PSSs and SSSC is essential for extracting the effect of combined operation. In this paper both PSS and SSSC are effectively coordinated by optimising their parameters using ACO algorithm. Also, this paper compares the stability of the test system with coordinated operation of PSS and SSSC using ACO and PSO algorithm. A two area multimachine system is taken as test system which is analysed under various operating conditions. The coordination of PSS and SSSC using ACO ensures a more stable operation under various operating conditions.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Low Power Long Range Protocol LoRaWAN for Embedded Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: LoRaWAN is a key technology for the Internet of Things. Generally, IoT application requires infrequent transmission of small data. The challenges in deploying wireless access technology for IoT are the deployment of large number of nodes and power constrained transmission. Among the available technologies, LoRaWAN ensures the ability to handle large number of nodes, less power consumption, longer transmission range and cheaper communication module. This paper presents a performance evaluation of LoRa network in respect to those claims. The work analyses the performance using network simulator ns3 and in real time. The performance study was carried out in terms of packet delivery ratio, received power per transmission, selection of spreading factor and communication range. The result shows that the performance of LoRa network depends highly on the selection of spreading factor, distance of the nodes from the gateway, communication channel and number of nodes. By analysing the results possible solutions to the existing challenges can be suggested.

articleTitle: Hybrid Compensation System using DSTATCOM and FCTCR for Enhanced Power Quality in AC Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Power quality issues pose significant challenges to electrical grids, impacting their reliability and efficiency. Issues such as voltage fluctuations, harmonic distortions, and reactive power imbalance can lead to equipment damage, increased energy consumption, and reduced system lifespan. Various solutions have been proposed to address these challenges, including the use of distribution static synchronous compensators (DSTATCOMs). DSTATCOMs are capable of dynamically compensating for reactive power, voltage fluctuations, and harmonics, thereby improving power quality in AC grids. However, despite their effectiveness, DSTATCOMs suffer from drawbacks such as high cost, and technical complexity. These factors can limit their widespread adoption and implementation in electrical grids, particularly in scenarios where cost and space are constrained. To overcome these limitations, a hybrid compensation system (HCS) integrating a fixed capacitor thyristor-controlled reactor (FCTCR) with DSTATCOM is proposed. In this hybrid configuration FCTCR is utilized to fulfill the reactive power requirements of the load, while DSTATCOM focuses solely on mitigating harmonics. By distributing the compensating tasks between FCTCR and DSTATCOM, the size, cost, and complexity of DSTATCOM are significantly reduced, making it a more attractive solution for enhancing power quality in AC grids. The entire system is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink and the performance of the system in improving the power quality is studied. Finally, a quantitative analysis has been done to analyze the improvement in sizing of DSTATCOM when it is combined with FCTCR.

articleTitle: Fault Detection in NPC Multilevel Inverter Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The evolution of power conversion technologies, particularly multilevel inverters, plays a crucial role in the efficiency and sustainability of renewable energy systems and electric vehicle (EV) drive trains. Despite their advanced capabilities in managing high power levels, the complex nature of multilevel inverters makes them prone to faults like open circuit faults, short circuit faults, and other faults, challenging their operational reliability. Traditional fault detection methods limited in scope and precision, fail to address the critical needs of these systems effectively. In response, this paper proposes an innovative Artificial Neural Network (ANN)-based approach for rapid and accurate fault detection of power switches within multilevel inverters. The paper mainly focuses on inverter power switch faults such as open circuit and short circuit fault detection. Utilizing dynamic learning and the adaptive capabilities of ANN, our method outperforms conventional techniques by providing robust fault diagnosis through detailed MATLAB simulations under varied operational scenarios. This approach not only enhances fault detection efficiency but also significantly contributes to maintaining the integrity of power conversion systems, highlighting the potential of advanced computational techniques in resolving maintenance and operational challenges in complex power electronic systems within a concise framework.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing Image Captioning using CNN and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Image captioning is a rapidly expanding field in computer vision research and it involves generating a comprehensive description for an input aerial image. The community has been paying more attention to it lately because it offers additional semantic information about images. To properly convey the connections between the objects and the features included in remote sensing pictures with their captions, this work proposes a system for captioning those images. The system is designed to generate and exploit textual descriptions. For captioning images, an encoder-decoder structure is employed. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are first used to encode the image’s visual properties. After that, the encoded features are sent to a language model, or decoder. For word by word descriptions of the image content, recurrent neural networks (RNNs), often referred to as long short term memory (LSTM), are commonly employed as language models. We combined the Bahdanau attention model with LSTM to enable learning to be focused on a specific region of the image to enhance performance. Four different pre-trained CNNs were evaluated for model performance in this study. Experimental results from UAVIC dataset are presented.

articleTitle: PV Array Reconfiguration Using Futoshiki Puzzle to Extract Maximum Power Under Partial Shading Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Solar Photovoltaic technology stands at the forefront among various renewable energy sources and experiencing widespread commercialization to meet the rising demand for electrical energy. The issue of partial shading poses a significant challenge in photovoltaic systems, impacting their energy yield substantially. This study explores the dispersion of shading through a static array reconfiguration technique, inspired by the principles of Futoshiki puzzles, for a 6x6 solar array. To evaluate the performance enhancements achieved by implementing Futoshiki-based array reconfiguration, a detailed theoretical calculation and its validation are provided through the MATLAB-SIMULINK simulation platform. A comprehensive evaluation, considering various performance indices such as fill factor, mismatch losses, performance ratio and enhanced power generation, emphasizes the effectiveness of the proposed technique in comparison to existing alternatives.

articleTitle: Enhancing Anomaly Detection in Sensor Time Series Data using Machine Learning Model Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Launch vehicles and satellites produce a substantial amount of sensor data primarily indented for monitoring and control applications. Human expertise plays an important role in interpreting the sensor data, detecting the anomalies, and making decisions to safeguard the underlying system, entails inherent operational risks. To reduce costs, automation using machine learning algorithms to enhance the identification of anomalies are presently employed, but it exhibits inaccuracies in its detection capabilities. Our investigation highlights the effectiveness of deep learning (DL) methods, including optimized architectures of ‘Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks’, in detecting anomalies, improving performance, and reducing computation time. In the scenario of anomaly detection, various techniques including regularization methods such as early stopping, additional dropout, and input dimensionality reduction are employed. The proposed architecture is realized and general effectiveness of the different architectures are compared using publicly accessible expert-labeled telemetry datasets. The performance of the baseline improves with the optimization approaches, as seen in the experimental results.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Different Rotor Structures In-Wheel Brushless DC Motor Performance for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The BLDC In-wheel motors are increasingly preferred for low-power electric vehicle applications due to their highly efficient mechanical energy conversion, high torque, and low maintenance compared to conventional BLDC motors. Additionally, they offer smooth operation, regenerative braking, and easy speed control. However, a key challenge in designing the rotor structure for in-wheel motors is managing heat, which can affect efficiency, and reliability, and lead to premature issues. This paper analyzes three different rotor flux barrier and skewing techniques aimed at minimizing losses and torque ripples. These techniques include surface-mounted radial magnets, surface-mounted parallel magnets, and surface-mounted multilayer radial magnets. Optimal geometry parameters are derived and calculated using sizing equations. A finite element model is employed to analyze motor solve software and study characteristics such as cogging torque, losses, and magnetic field strength. Simulation results demonstrate that the interior rotor curved magnet in-wheel motor enhances performance to meet the requirements for low-power electric vehicles. The surface-mounted radial magnet rotor structure achieves less cogging torque and high efficiency for in-wheel motor EV applications.

articleTitle: Optimized Machine Learning Model for Disease Prediction and Treatment Recommendation Through Gait Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This research introduces an advanced machine learning model for disease prediction and treatment recommendations, leveraging gait analysis as a primary input. Using a diverse dataset encompassing various health conditions, the model employs state-of-the-art feature extraction and optimization techniques to accurately predict underlying health conditions. Beyond disease prediction, it incorporates a treatment recommendation component, generating personalized suggestions based on gait analysis. Rigorous testing demonstrates the model's robustness and significant improvements in disease prediction accuracy and treatment recommendation precision compared to existing approaches. In conclusion, this cutting-edge model enhances early intervention and patient outcomes through comprehensive gait analysis for disease prediction and personalized treatment recommendations. Overall, our work underscores the immense potential of optimized machine learning models in harnessing the power of gait analysis for disease prediction and treatment recommendation. By bridging the gap between data-driven insights and clinical decision-making, we aim to empower healthcare professionals with innovative tools for enhancing patient care and improving health outcomes.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis in Three Phase Long Transmission Lines using Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Fault classification require an analysis and identification of the type of fault on a transmission line. The discrete wavelet transform is employed to identify the fault type and identify the fault's occurrence phase. During a fault, the current waveform is utilized to identify the fault. This paper presents a simple fault detection mechanism that can be applied to computer relaying applications. To produce fault signals, a simulation is conducted using MATLAB Simulink. This paper presents an algorithm that can detect fault at any location throughout the transmission line along with the change of the load parameters. This algorithm is also capable of fault classification and detection of faulted phase.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Reconfiguration Techniques Used to Reduce Partial Shading Losses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Exhaustion of fossil fuels and environmental damage drive the search for renewable energy options. Solar photovoltaic energy, a sustainable source, is controlled by sunlight levels. Partial shade results in reduced sun irradiation, leading to decreased power generation and multiple electrical peaks requiring advanced strategies to extract maximum power. This study compares the performance of reconfiguration methods for partial shading mitigation, including SDK, OE-TCT, LS-TCT, and TCT using MATLAB/Simulink simulation results. Performance metrics include power enhancement ratio, partial shading loss, performance ratio, and fill factor.

articleTitle: High Gain Multiport Boost Converter for Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: In the current situation, facilitating the incorporation of renewable energy is imperative. A single renewable source is not enough to make any system work for more time. This paper focuses on addressing these challenges to adopt hybrid renewable energy sources by proposing a high gain multiport boost converter tailored for hybrid renewable energy sources. The paper details the mathematical modelling of a multiport boost converter, with solar cells and FC stack. The closed loop output voltage of the multiport boost converter is regulated with the decoupler controller for different load variations. The model undergoes simulation to verify its performance and efficiency.

articleTitle: Analysis and Prediction of the Events Occurring in the Scaled Down Model of IEEE 5 Bus System using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The power system grid around the world is dealing with enormous amount of electrical and nonelectrical data every day. This big data carry large amount of information which need to be analysed using novel algorithms and technologies, to unleash the potential of these data, which can revolutionize the power system operation, planning and scheduling. This paper proposes a Machine Learning model which train on the IEEE 5 bus data set to predict the events occurring in the system. The data acquisition is done from the scaled down model of the IEEE 5 bus system. The data is pre-processed and analyzed using classification models. The efficacy of the models is assessed using evaluation metrics and a comparison is made for the performance of models, when feature selection is done.

articleTitle: Intelligent Rush Hour Management in Metro Station
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Addressing the issue of high crowd density in metro stations during rush hours is indeed a significant challenge, but innovative solutions can help enhance passenger experience and streamline the boarding process. The goal is to implement a Smart Crowd Management System that provides real-time information about congestion levels in metro stations and estimates the time required for passengers to board trains during peak hours. The implementation of a Smart Crowd Management System can significantly improve the passenger experience in metro stations, making the commute more efficient and less stressful during rush hours. This proposal outlines a holistic approach combining sensor technology, machine learning, digital communication, and mobile applications to address the challenges of crowd density in metropolitan cities like Delhi. In this work, an intelligent system is developed with MATLAB/Simulink interface having fuzzy logic and neural network classifier to indicate expected time of departure and degree of congestion in the station. The outputs are displayed in TFT screen, LEDs and ThingSpeak-IoT platform.

articleTitle: IoT Based Food and Grain Condition Traceability and Controlling System in Warehouses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: India, a predominantly agrarian nation with 70% of its population engaged in farming, emphasizes the significance of grain storage and food security for national economic strength. Atmospheric factors such as temperature, humidity, and carbon dioxide concentration profoundly impact stored grain quality in warehouses. This paper presents a real-time grain storage monitoring system utilizing DHT22, MQ135, Peltier module, flame sensor, ultrasonic repellant, and PIR sensors, grounded in IoT principles. The project incorporates features like online detection, control mechanisms, and systematic updates. Temperature regulation through the Peltier module aids in pinpointing locations affected by food spoilage, enhancing farming practices. Machine learning techniques contribute to animal control, adjusting ultrasonic repeller frequencies based on detected animal presence. Predictive analysis through machine learning anticipates future readings, elevating the quality standard for stored grains. The primary goal is to minimize grain wastage, reduce manpower, and eliminate constant manual oversight.

articleTitle: A Hardware Efficient Implementation of Sub-Block Interleaver for Polar Codes in 5G NR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: In the fast-paced realm of Fifth-Generation (5G) and next-generation wireless technologies, the pursuit of efficiency and speed reaches new heights. Amidst the complexity of implementing error correcting codes, lies a daunting challenge to achieve reduced resource utilization and low latency without compromising performance. Hence the emphasis of this work is to reduce the latency and resource utilization of sub-block interleaving process used in the rate-matching of polar codes in 5G NR. The implementation of the modulus division function and the floor function in sub-block interleaving of polar codes to obtain the interleaved address is quite a difficult task. To address this challenge, this paper presents a novel Counter Based Sub-block interleaver (CBS) architecture for polar codes, suitable for 5G and beyond applications. A computationally less intensive and high-speed sub-block interleaver is proposed based on a simple algorithm, eliminating a few intricate arithmetic components, and generating the sub-block interleaved address. The proposed architecture is simulated for downlink and uplink channel specifications in MATLAB and Vivado design suite to verify the functionality of the design. For fair comparison, the proposed CBS for uplink and downlink channels is synthesized in Virtex-7 FPGA. The implementation results reveal that the proposed CBS achieves an 83% reduction in average resource utilization for the PDCCH channel compared to the existing implementations. The proposed CBS is 7.51 times faster than the conventional architecture. The CBS architecture is tested on Artix-7 (Basys-3) Board.

articleTitle: Investigating FPGA optimization methods for the performance evaluation of SKINNY cipher
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Hardware optimization of lightweight ciphers is essential for maximizing resource efficiency and performance in resource-constrained environments like IoT devices, ensuring secure and energy-efficient cryptographic operations. This paper investigates Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) optimization techniques tailored for lightweight cryptography, focusing on the lightweight, tweakable block cipher SKINNY. Three different optimization strategies are investigated via round-based and byte-serial implementations: S-box optimization, combining ShiftRow and MixColumns operations, and integrating former optimizations. Utilizing an Artix-7 FPGA board, the study evaluates performance metrics including resource utilization, power consumption, timing analysis, and operating frequency. Results indicate significant reductions in power consumption, particularly notable within byte-serial architectures, with the proposed method showcasing up to a 41.8% reduction. Offering important insights into hardware optimization for cryptographic primitives, the work proposes the suggested method as an effective FPGA optimization strategy for lightweight block ciphers across both round-based and byte-serial architectures.

articleTitle: Implementation of Silicon Wafer Defect Classification Web application using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This paper presents a solution for the wafers classification of defected silicon wafers, a critical task in semiconductor manufacturing processes. The classification aims to identify various patterns of defects which are pivotal for quality control. The presented approach in this paper leverages deep learning techniques, employing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Autoencoders, to automatically learn discriminative features from wafer map images. The trained model is then serialized into a pickle file for efficient deployment and integration. To democratize access to the solution, a user-friendly web interface is developed using Flask, enabling seamless interaction with the classification model. Users can upload wafer map images through the web page, and in return, receive real-time predictions of the defect class, facilitating quick decision-making in manufacturing processes. The presented method demonstrates promising results, achieving high accuracy in classifying defected silicon wafers across diverse patterns. This contributes significantly to enhancing the efficiency and reliability of semiconductor manufacturing, ultimately leading to improved product quality and reduced production costs.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Charging System for Electric Vehicle with Improved Power Quality
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) connected to the electric grid can not only recharge its own battery but can also feed energy back into the grid referred to as vehicle-to-grid (V2G). This technique helps to reduce peak load, regulating voltage, balancing of the load and increase the stability of power system. In this paper a battery electric vehicle (BEV) was utilized for both charging and discharging power. Bidirectional power transfer is accomplished through a bidirectional DC-DC converter and a single-phase full bridge inverter. This topology can minimize the harmonic distortion of the grid-injected current and keep it within standards. The control method proposed in this paper provides the user with the flexibility to select the operational mode of the circuit. Simulation of this system is verified in MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Compressor based Approximate Multipliers for Neural Network Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: As several image and video processing applications gain popularity, the approximate computing has gained importance to effectively utilize the available channel bandwidth. As multipliers are the computationally intensive components of neural networks, the aim of this paper remains to approximate it and reduce the number of components utilized for its implementation. This paper proposes six approximate multipliers based on approximation of 4 to 2 compressors for Neural Networks. The design 1 utilizes exact 8x8 multiplier with 2, 3 and 4-input AND, XOR and OR gates for approximate compressor with 6.25% error, The design 2 utilizes only 2-input XOR, AND and OR gates for approximate compressor with 37.5% error. The designs 3 to 6 are the combinations of multiplexer based approximations carried out with an error of `5.8% to 20%. The designs are developed in Verilog HDL and implemented for 28nm high-K CMOS technology based Zynq FPGA (XC7Z100-2FFG1156) in Xilinx Vivado Tool. The proposed design 5 proves to be reliable along with the less total path delay of at least by 2.47% to 7.81% and the power dissipation being minimum by at least 5.6% to 14.02%. How ever design 5 trades off area by 2.98% to 6.94%, where design 6 proves to be a good choice. From results, the proposed designs 5 and 6 to be good choice for approximate multipliers.

Author Keywords: Approximate Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor technology

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of 100MW Floating Solar PV System: A Idukki Reservoir Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This paper explores the potential of a 100 MWp floating photovoltaic (FPV) system at Kerala’s Idukki Reservoir, leveraging PVsyst, Global Solar Atlas, and Meteonorm 8.0 data. By modeling the FPV system’s performance in line with reservoir features and regional sunlight, we find an average normalized output of 165,974,766 kWh/kWp/year. Moreover, the system reduces CO2 emissions by 3,833,762.0 tons, offering valuable insights into its performance and energy generation potential above water bodies.

articleTitle: Design of Low Power and High Speed 1-bit Full Adder for DSP Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This paper deals with the design of the full adder circuit using the Cadence virtuoso 180nm technology. The entire circuit of the full adder consists of generation of XOR- XNOR, sum and carry. The adder is implemented in such a way that it meets the specifications of full voltage output swing and less delay. The performance of the full adder is observed using the cadence tool. The circuit contains the characteristics of the novel circuit which is really essential in order to gain the utilization of it in real life applications.

articleTitle: BAT-CNN: BirdNet Assisted Training for CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Studies on bird sound classification have become increasingly popular in recent years. Birds serve as valuable ecological indicators, and the threat to bird species populations is a serious concern. The emergence of artificial intelligence has been a milestone in species classification, making the classification easier and more accurate. For the acoustic classification of bird species, a number of works have been reported in the literature but there are still challenges. In this, we propose a deep learning approach for bird sound classification. A dataset consisting of recordings of 10 bird species is used for classification. The dataset is sourced from recordings on the Xenocanto website. Many bird audio recordings are available for studying their existence, but classifying these recordings is challenging due to the overlapping calls from multiple birds. A different approach is used in the proposed work for preprocessing the downloaded audio. BirdNet, which can recognize over 6500 birds, is employed for separating the audio of the corresponding species from the overlappings of the multiple species present in the downloaded audio files. The BirdNet separated recordings of the 10 species are then converted into spectrograms. The obtained spectrograms are then fed into a CNN model for classification. The model achieved an average accuracy of 90% for the ten bird species.

articleTitle: Enhancing Electric Vehicle Charger Efficiency Through Improved PQ-Based Zeta-Luo Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Electric Vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure is significantly advanced by introducing a novel charger that employs an improved Power Quality (PQ)-based Zeta-Luo converter. By merging the strengths of Zeta and Luo converters into a seamless bridgeless topology, this innovative approach not only optimizes charging efficiency but also ensures stable charging currents, addressing a crucial need within the rapidly expanding EV market. The charger operates in Discontinuous Conduction Mode (DCM), a strategy that significantly enhances power quality at the output, meeting the stringent demands of modern power electronics. Extensive simulations conducted in MATLAB/Simulink illustrate the operational advantages of the proposed system, highlighting a reduced component count, reduced harmonics, and compliance with rigorous power quality standards. The results of this study underscore the immense potential of combining Zeta and Luo converters to achieve significant efficiency improvements in EV charging systems by achieving the power factor pre-regulation.

articleTitle: Level Shifted PODPWM Technique for Quadra Boost Nine Level Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Introducing a novel Quadra boost switched capacitor inverter (QBSCI) a simplified component design. This innovative topology utilizes only eight switches and one DC source can generate a nine-level output using important features like quadruple boost functionality, and the capability to handle inductive loads. This results in enhanced overall cost-effectiveness in comparison with other multilevel inverters using switching capacitors (SCMLIs). As compared to traditional SCMLIs, the suggested QBSCI eliminates the back-end H-bridge, simplifying the overall design.

articleTitle: ECG Denoising: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Different Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is extensively used in diagnosing cardiovascular conditions. The electrical activity of the heart is recorded by an electrocardiogram (ECG), yet noise interference can cause problems. ECG signal denoising is a crucial initial step that reduces noise and enhances the prominent waves in ECG signals. The weight settings of the adaptive filtering method significantly affect the efficiency of the output signal while denoising ECG signals. However, a significant challenge with adaptive filters is the need to adjust a large number of parameters. Heuristic algorithms, known for their ability to solve a wide range of optimization problems, are particularly effective in addressing such complexities. An optimization method usually seeks to minimise an objective function that quantifies the difference between the noisy and clean signal. In this paper, we investigate the effectiveness of four different optimization algorithms for denoising ECG signals: the Least Mean Square (LMS) filter, Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Snake Optimization (SO), and Adaptive Fish Migration Optimization (AFMO). The ECG signals are taken from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia database for the project. Parameters like the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), the error between the original and denoised signals, and the Peak Root Mean Square Difference (PRD) are used to gauge how well the algorithms function.

articleTitle: PV fed Off-board E-bike Battery Charger using LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: In this paper, a PV-fed off-board e-bike battery charging system using an inductor-inductor capacitor (LLC) resonant converter is presented. The resonant LLC converters are preferred these days for electric vehicle (EV) battery charging applications for their better characteristics in terms of higher efficiency, galvanic isolation, higher power density, low electromagnetic interference (EMI), wide input voltage range, and soft switching characteristics. The proposed charger consists of a LLC converter with a controllable rectifier. The closed-loop control is applied for the charger using the doubleloop PI control strategy. The control includes a Constant Current- Constant Voltage (CC-CV) charging and zero voltage switching (ZVS). The charger topology is studied and analyzed using MATLAB/Simulink. The designed topology can be adapted for efficient charging of e-bikes using solar energy.

articleTitle: Air Quality Prediction using Deep Learning models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: In today's world, air pollution is an important concern for both the general public and the environment. Monitoring and forecasting pollutant concentrations in the environment is critical to effective pollution control and management. Using advanced deep-learning techniques, this study focuses on the development of a time series air quality prediction (AQP) model for numerous pollutants in the air, including small particles of PM2.5, PM10, ground-level ozone (O3), carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO2), and nitrogen dioxide (NO2). Time series data are used in the study to capture temporal relationships and seasonal trends inherent in air quality measurements. This proposed AQP model evaluates many deep learning architectures, such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Bidirectional LSTM (Bi- LSTM). This study demonstrates how effective these models are at capturing temporal dependencies and seasonal patterns in air quality datasets, pointing towards novel approaches for precise and timely air quality monitoring. The results of this research provide a substantial contribution to the advancement of air quality prediction systems, allowing for better decision- making for public health and environmental protection.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Textile Substrates adopted in Wearable Antennas: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This article is presented with the review of various textile substrates material that has been utilized in designing wearable textile antennas. The existing review articles presented had analysed several frequently used textile substrates like Jeans, Denim and Cotton. In this article, the performances of peculiar textile substrates like Silk, PF4 foam, Polyester, Felt and other unique substrates like Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), Tween, Lycra, etc. are studied in detail through the significant parameters of textile antenna such as gain, radiation efficiency and Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) value. For detailed analogy, along with these substrates several frequently used substrates like Denim, Jeans, Cotton and Polymide are also considered. After comparison of various textile substrates in recent research articles, it is noted that Felt exposes excellent performance in ISM band. The maximum gain and radiation efficiency exhibited by the Felt material in ISM band is 9.2dBi and 83% respectively; minimum SAR value obtained by the Felt material is 0.014 W/Kg for one gram capacity of tissue and 0.47 W/Kg for ten gram capacity of tissue which is under the limit according to standards.

articleTitle: Optimizing Communication in High-Speed Train Environments over 5G Signals through MIMO Base Station Positioning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The next big thing in mobile communication is 5G technology. With the incredibly high data rates that this technology offers, users can access the Internet of Things, HD live video conferences, and other features. With today's train technology, a high-speed train (HST) can travel at up to 300 km/h. There will be a lot of passengers moving quickly, so if they use 5G technology for mobile communication, they could encounter service interruptions and problems with data rates when they move. This paper aims to enhance data transmission rates for HST users by addressing the heightened penetration loss associated with 5G communication at high speeds. This is achieved through the implementation of multiple input and multiple output (MIMO), beam-forming techniques, and related strategies. To mitigate penetration loss, we integrate the HST communication system with an indoor-outdoor antenna configuration, enabling users within the train to receive signals from the internal wireless network. Signals, characterized by high directivity and directed toward users, are transmitted using a narrow beam-width antenna. The beam directionality is achieved through beam steering or switching mechanisms, which track user movements. The global positioning system (GPS) data from the mobile relay antenna determines the precise location of the high-speed train. This paper addresses both the train speed and user data rate, emphasizing the utilization of directed beams tailored for HST communication.

articleTitle: Artificial Neural Network Based Fault Identification and Monitoring for Brushless Direct Current Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: As the electric vehicle (EV) industry advances, guaranteeing the dependability and security of crucial components like inverters, brushless DC (BLDC) motors, and battery packs is essential to avoid malfunctions and safeguard passengers. This research focuses on enhancing the safety and dependability of electric vehicles by continuously monitoring their operational conditions and detecting failures early. Given the complexity of early failure detection, which involves navigating through intricate processes and addressing unpredictability, our study leverages artificial neural networks (ANNs) to facilitate effective real-time problem detection and implement fault-tolerant controls. Our work in this field involves a comprehensive examination of problems that could impact motors in electric vehicles, along with the creation of an effective fault detection system to address these issues. This paper introduces novel fault identification and diagnostic methods tailored for EV motors, tackling problems such as open and short circuit faults, sensor malfunctions, and fluctuations in temperature. Utilizing Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), our methodology provides a rapid, accurate, sensitive, and cost-effective solution for ensuring the reliable operation of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Medical Image Fusion Techniques: A Variety of Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The goal of medical image fusion is to combine complementary data from several imaging modalities to improve research, diagnosis, and therapy and research by integrating complementary data gathered from several imaging modalities. In this research, Four distinct methodologies are used in this study to investigate medical image fusion: Laplacian re-decomposition (LRD) fusion methodology, Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Simple Average, and Multi-Level Morphological Gradient Pulse Coupled Neural Network (MLMG PCNN).

articleTitle: Improved Pulse Coupled Neural Network based on Maximize SNR for Vessel Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of branch loss and fracture in the fundus retinal vessel segmentation algorithm, with improved pulsed coupled neural network (PCNN) is proposed. As the matched filter can maximize the signal to noise ratio even though using the gaussian filter, therefore, it is used for reducing the noise. First, matching filters are used to enhance the retinal image, and then a segmentation algorithm is suggested using a combination of matching filter and PCNN. Finally, the evaluation on DRIVE database demonstrates that the sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of the algorithm are 0.7310, 0.9640, and 0.9711 accordingly compared with other algorithms. Simulation experiments illustrate that the Matched-PCNN algorithm resolves the effect of low light and optic disc highlight on vessel segmentation, and demonstrates good connectivity between blood vessels.

articleTitle: An Improvised Antenna for Wireless Implantable Medical Devices (WIMD) that support Retinal Prosthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Retinal diseases represent some of the top causes of blindness reported by the WHO. According to the survey planned by the Government of India in the country blindness caused by treatable diseases is about 68%, preventable diseases 25% , and remaining 7% unavoidable diseases. An artificial vision system will help to reduce the percentage of blindness.This paper presents an improvised design of an antenna for wireless implantable medical devices (WIMD) that support retinal prosthesis. The proposed microstrip patch antenna design has a ground, main radiator, and parasitic structure with a modified square ring, mitered cross, and splitting four arms with an emptied channel that features circular polarization and Industrial, Scientific, and Medical(ISM) band working frequency supporting high data rate could improve the image perception capability. Biocompatible material Roger 6010 reduces the size and toxicity of the implant.The proposed model was designed and simulated using High-frequency simulation software (HFSS). A scaled version of the prototype antenna was fabricated with a flexible copper sheet, it was found that the prototype antenna embedded in minced pork results satisfactorily matched the simulated version.

articleTitle: AI-assisted Silhouettes Generation from Sparse mmWave Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach leveraging the U-Net algorithm to generate silhouette images of objects using sparse data generated by computers or obtained from mmWave radar. Through this method, exceptional replication of previously unseen images is achieved. The implementation of this algorithm holds significant potential for applications such as collision avoidance on roads or runway incursion. By harnessing sparse data and the power of deep learning, this approach offers promising prospects for enhancing safety measures in various domains.

articleTitle: Modeling and Control of SEPIC Converters in Hybrid Microgrid Application using Exact Linearization Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: In order to provide energy for irrigation, electric motors, lighting, and other uses, hybrid systems are becoming more and more necessary in rural microgrids. For usage in a microgrid based on solar energy and wind energy, where nonlinear converters are employed, this work describes the application of an exact linearization technique for the modeling and control of a SEPIC converter. Wind and solar energy modules are harvested by a single-ended primary inductor converter (SEPIC), and the energy flow between the battery and the grid is controlled by a bidirectional buckboost converter, which permits battery charging and discharging. The exact linearization theory designed for power converters is applied to both units. By linearizing the converter model, this technique essentially allows for the consideration of various operating points under various conditions. This work offers a comprehensive overview of the implemented microgrid topology and includes experimental results to highlight the effectiveness of the proposed control system.

articleTitle: Interleaved Boost PFC with Half Bridge LLC Resonant Converter based EV Battery Charger
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Electric scooters are attaining demand over conventional ICE scooters due to increases in fuel costs, depletion of fossil fuels, and reduced maintenance in EVs. This paper presents a 1kW two-stage onboard charger consisting of an interleaved boost PFC converter in the primary stage and a half-bridge LLC resonant converter at the secondary stage. The PFC stage maintains a voltage of 310V which is regulated to charge a 60V 86Ah electric scooter battery by the LLC resonant converter. The converter PFC stage is operated in discontinuous conduction mode to achieve natural power factor correction reduce the burden of implementation of complex control circuits and increase the reliability of the converter. The half-bridge topology in the secondary stage reduces the number of switches required without affecting the efficiency of the converter. The secondary stage converter is further operated in zero voltage switching mode to reduce the switching losses. The simulation results show that the system can perform satisfactorily achieving power factor correction and managing the THD level at acceptable limits for EV battery chargers.

Author Keywords: Interleaved Boost Converter. Power Factor Correction

articleTitle: Deep - Transfer Learning for Multi-Crop Leaf Disease prediction using ResNet and ConvNet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Plant diseases can be categorized based on the nature of their primary causal agents, either infectious or noninfectious. The detection and identification of such plant diseases play a critical role in sustaining agricultural productivity and preventing crop losses. Manual disease tracking is a labor-intensive, knowledge-dependent, and time-consuming task. To address these challenges, Deep-TL (Deep Transfer Learning) techniques are used to capture plant leaf images and compare them with extensive datasets representing various plants. This paper suggests a model that makes use of the capabilities of deep learning algorithms, particularly those trained on large datasets, such as ResNet (Residual Networks) and ConvNet (Convolutional Neural Networks). Through the use of transfer learning strategies, the Deep-TL model gains better accuracy and performance by utilising the knowledge gained and achieved the accuracy of 98.2%.

articleTitle: Smart Farming: Integrating Soil Monitoring and Weather Analysis for Precision Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Soil and weather conditions are foundational to agriculture, collectively influencing crop growth and productivity. This project proposes a comprehensive system that integrates soil and weather analysis to support precision farming. The system focuses on monitoring essential soil parameters such as moisture content, temperature, electrical conductivity, pH levels, and concentrations of key nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium alongside crucial weather data. Using open source hardware suitable for field deployment, the system allows farmers to remotely access data through mobile devices or PCs. This dual focus on soil and weather enables farmers to make more informed decisions about agricultural practices. Additionally, the system utilizes machine learning algorithms to predict crops based on soil and weather parameters, aiding in optimizing farming strategies and thereby enhancing overall agricultural productivity.

articleTitle: Adaptive Common-Mode Voltage Reduction Technique for Three Level NPC Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Common Mode Voltage (VCOMO) created by space vector pulse width modulated inverters induces bearing currents that causes premature motor bearing failure, induces electromagnetic interference (EMI) and breaks down motor winding insulation. In this paper, an Adaptive Common Mode Voltage Reduction (ACMoR) method is proposed for space vector pulse width modulated three level neutral point clamped (NPC-3L) inverters. Common Mode Voltage Sense and Cascaded H-bridge power circuit system used in ACMoR reduces the VCOMO that arises between the motor neutral point and the dc link return of NPC-3L inverter, irrespective of the space vectors selected, thus enhancing the dc bus utilisation. Simulation results show a significant reduction in VCOMO with ACMoR method, when a three-phase load is driven by a NPC-3L inverter.

articleTitle: Yoga Pose Classification Using CNN with PReLU Activation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This research uses the power of machine learning for yoga pose classification. A convolutional neural network (CNN) solution for Yoga Pose estimation is proposed in this research. This approach is firmly grounded on a diverse dataset sourced from Kaggle, comprising five quintessential yoga poses - Downdog, Goddess, Plank, Tree, and Warrior2. The distinguishing feature of this model lies in the evaluation of various activation functions namely, Sigmoid, Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) and Parametric Rectified Linear Unit (PReLU) and found PReLU giving the expected results. This evaluation lends flexibility to the network and augments its learning ability. The final architecture of Yoga Pose Prodigy was designed, encompassing convolutional layers, PReLU activations, max-pooling layers, and densely connected layers. The pivotal layer leads to a five-unit output layer, employing the softmax activation for precise multi-class classification. In the quest for optimal performance, the proposed model undergoes rigorous training, validation, and testing phases. During this process, the proposed system attains a remarkable accuracy of 97.8%, marking a significant milestone in the realm of yoga pose recognition.

articleTitle: Floating-point CORDIC Coprocessor with Dynamic Iterations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: In this paper a detailed description is provided for computing of sine, cosine and atan for both single and double precision floating point using dynamic iterations of CORDIC algorithm. The iterations needed for computing a function are decided in real time based on the input value. A detailed emphasis is given on the validity and advantages of this method. Also, the computation of the above functions is done by the linear terms of the Taylor series expansion in their respective valid domains both for the ease of implementation and to confine the number of maximum iterations. The size of the hardware (shifters, adders, atan table) required for the above implementation is derived and justified. The results of these theoretical derivations are coded in VHDL and simulation was carried out. The floating-point results match with Intel processor outputs up to 1 LS bit mismatch. The hardware module of CORDIC was interfaced to custom processor which is having micro code-based control unit. New set of instructions were incorporated in the microcode to support the trigonometric operations. With this compute module hardware implementation, a 17-times reduction in the clock cycle required for the computation of the above functions was achieved.

articleTitle: Evaluating Reliability: A Comparative Analysis of Two High Gain DC to DC Converters in Solar Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: DC micro grids are optimisable solution for bounded energy distribution due to their high reliability and efficiency. In Solar Photo-voltaic systems(SP-VS) based DC microgrids, High Gain Step-up DC to DC Converters (HGSDDC) are essential for effectively regulating energy transfer. They are intended to convert 20-40v dc to 380-400v dc with maximum efficiency with low input ripple current. To obtain high gain, several topologies have been proposed based on voltage multiplier circuits, coupled inductor circuits, and voltage lift methods or with their combinations. Reliability of these converters affect sustainability of the entire DC micro grid system. Component level thermal performance can be used to rate the reliability of a converter. In this paper, we delve into the thermal performance and reliability assessment of two recently proposed HGSDDCs. These converters have garnered attention due to their high gain and efficiency. Modelling and simulation is performed using PLECS. The simulation results demonstrate the high reliability of coupled inductor(CI) based HGSDDC2. The only negative aspect of this converter is the high reverse voltage of its output diode. Reducing the high voltage stress on diodes will significantly increase converter life and, consequently, system reliability.

Author Keywords: High Gain Step up DC to DC converters

articleTitle: Speed Control of Three-Phase Induction Motor Using ANFIS and Flower Pollination Algorithm Optimized PI Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach for the speed control of a three-phase induction motor by integrating an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) with a Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA) optimized Proportional-Integral (PI) controller. The primary objective is to improve the efficiency of induction motor speed control under various load conditions, ensuring robustness and adaptability. The ANFIS is employed to intelligently predict and adjust the motor speed in real-time, capitalizing on its ability to handle nonlinearities and uncertainties inherent in the motor dynamics. To further refine the control strategy, the PI controller's parameters are optimized using the Flower Pollination Algorithm, a nature-inspired optimization technique that mimics the pollination process of flowers. This optimization ensures that the PI controller works in perfect harmony with the FPA model, resulting in improved response times, minimized speed overshoot, and enhanced stability under dynamic load changes. Simulation results exhibit the superiority of the proposed method over traditional control strategies, offering significant improvements in speed control accuracy and system resilience. The FPA-PI outperforms the ANFIS based control and provides effective speed control of the motor.

articleTitle: Design of Co-Planar Waveguide Fed Split Ring Resonator Loaded Diamond Shaped Antenna for Industrial Scientific Medical Radio Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This paper presents a coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed metamaterial or split-ring resonator (SRR) inspired diamond ring with a trident patch antenna designed for industrial scientific medical radio band (ISM) and Fifth Generation (5G) applications. The antenna is premeditated on an FR4 substrate of dimension 20mm× 20mm× 1.6mm and produces three frequency bands. The simulated results show a reflection coefficient of 14dB at 2.4GHz, 17dB at 4.5GHz, and 20dB at 5.7GHz frequencies. This CPW-fed SRR-inspired triple-band antenna has high gain and bandwidth which is highly suited for ISM and 5G applications.

articleTitle: A Coplanar Wave Guide Fed Triangular Shaped Implantable Antenna for Industrial Scientific Medical Radio Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This paper presents a conductor-backed coplanar waveguide (CB-CPW) fed triple circular and triangular-shaped antenna for industrial medical service (ISM) band applications. The designed antenna consists of three circular and triangle-shaped patches with muscle layers. The designed patch has a micro-size of dimension 0.02λo×0.02λo×0.003λo. The return losses are 19dB for with tissue and 18dB for without tissue obtained at an ISM-based resonance frequency of 5.8GHz. The foremost advantages of this model are micro size, high gain, and bandwidth. The designed antenna is constructed by an FR-4 substrate. The standard parametric result of this designed prototype model indicated that this is the best device for ISM band (5.7-5.8GHz) based healthcare monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Improving User Satisfaction for Next Generation CRN using Utility Proportional Fairness based Resource Allocation Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: As the wireless traffic requirements have been increasing daily, it is tedious task to satisfy all users with the available resources. In this work, an effort has been made to allocate resource blocks (RB), satisfactorily to various users in a Cognitive Radio Network (CRN) for downlink transmission. An inter-band mode of Carrier Aggregation (CA) technology is used for this framework and it is simulated by aggregating 60 MHz bandwidth of n77 band with 100 MHz bandwidth of n40 band within the FR1 band. The proposed work aims to improve the satisfaction at the individual and network levels in a cognitive radio-based network. The analysis of satisfaction is done with the help of different utility functions. Here the gNodeB (base station) acts as a centralized unit which allows the secondary (unlicensed) users to opportunistically use the chance to get served by gNodeB in the absence of primary (licensed) users. The simulation results show that proposed system provides comparatively higher throughput for its users and a 76% improvement in the overall system satisfaction (OSS) compared to conventional weighted proportional fairness policy method.

articleTitle: Experimental Validation of Mathematical Modeling of MoX Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Controlling air pollution requires a systematic approach, including the establishment of a reliable air quality monitoring system. This work suggests experimenting with the mathematical modeling of metal oxide sensors and its validation to enhance the accuracy of air pollutant measurements, thereby supporting more effective strategies for pollution control and safeguarding human health and the environment. The use of MQ series gas sensors for individual pollutant measurement poses a risk of deviation from actual values due to cross-sensitivity and humidity factors. The mathematical model is derived from fundamental equations, including the Freundlich isotherm, with the aim of predicting the sensor’s characteristics. By utilizing this model, it is expected that the sensor’s performance and its ability to detect changes in pollutant concentrations will be improved. A mathematical model has been created to forecast the reaction of the MQ series sensor. To confirm the effectiveness of the approach, the modeled and original data curves are extensively compared with experimental data from the different experimental setups. Through the experimental setups and the comparison of data with original curves, the model’s ability to predict dynamic changes in gas concentrations based on sensor readings is validated. The versatility of the model was evident in its consistent application across different sensors. Thus, the model proves to be suitable for predicting the response of the MQ series sensor.

articleTitle: Advancements in the Efficacy of Flan-T5 for Abstractive Text Summarization: A Multi-Dataset Evaluation Using ROUGE and BERTScore
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This research ventured into the realm of abstractive text summarization, focusing on the amalgamation and efficacy of sophisticated NLP models, notably Flan-T5. We employed these cutting-edge models on a variety of datasets, such as XSum, CNN/DailyMail, Multi-News, Newsroom, and Gigaword, to gauge their summarization abilities. The models' performance was assessed using complex metrics like ROUGE and BERTScore. A remarkable discovery was the attainment of a ROUGE-L score of 0.5021 on the Gigaword dataset, underscoring the models' proficiency in producing coherent and contextually precise summaries. The outcomes were substantial, indicating a noticeable improvement in the quality, coherence, and contextual accuracy of the summaries generated by these models. This study concludes that the application of Flan-T5 signifies a considerable progression in the field of abstractive text summarization. Their capacity to effectively process and abridge extensive information is a reflection of their technological capability and constitutes a significant step forward in NLP, opening up new avenues for data processing and knowledge dissemination.

articleTitle: Automatic Rotary Assembly Line Speed Controller and Fault Detection System using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The project is designed for Automatic Rotary Assembly Line Speed control and Fault Detection System using Machine Learning algorithm. The Machine Learning algorithm is used to improve the accuracy of the proposed system. The modified SVM machine learning algorithm has improved the accuracy of the system. The accuracy of the system is 94.8%. It is also a fault detection system to detect the quality of product by measuring the height and weight of the product at the end of the chain (for example Bread packets). In small scale industry the conveyor system is manual and worker keep doing monotonous tasks. With time their efficiency decreases and chance of error increases. So most of time many defected products get supplied to the supply chain and leads to the negative image of the industry therefore causes loss of the valuable customers. To avoid the situation we propose the system to detect the faulty products at the final stage of manufacturing. Purpose of project is to detect the fault in the height and weight of product. If the quality of product decreases, there will be loss in company’s account. It will segregate the faulty and non-faulty product into two different boxes using a servo mechanism.

articleTitle: DAB based advanced EV Charging System for V2G Mode Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The rising demand for renewable energy and energy storage facilities, driven by the depletion of conventional energy sources, underscores the importance of projects aimed at integrating plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs) as energy storage systems. This project facilitates energy storage by charging PEV batteries during low-demand hours and supplying power back to the grid during peak-demand hours. When connected to an electrical grid, PEVs can operate in two different modes: Grid-to-Vehicle (G2V) mode and Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) mode. In G2V mode, the vehicle’s battery is charged from the grid, while in V2G mode, the battery supplies power back to the grid. This paper presents the design and analysis of a DAB-based advanced charging system for V2G mode operation. A PEV charging control scheme with bidirectional power flow capability is developed using a proportional-integral (PI) controller. This proposed control strategy is tested in a system model comprising an electrical grid, bidirectional converters, filters, and lithium-ion batteries. The designed system model is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink, and the controller’s performance in both operating modes is evaluated and validated.

articleTitle: Lattice thermal conductivity of material and its correlation with Debye temperature using regression models
