publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Lattice thermal conductivity (K) of the material plays a crucial role in its variety of applications such as thermoelectric, thermal barrier coating and so on. The role of the Debye temperature (T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>) is a significant factor in determining the lattice thermal conductivity of any materials. However, the relation between the lattice thermal conductivity and Debye temperature is very less explored using Machine Learning (ML). In this study, we first predicted lattice thermal conductivity using four machine learning regression models: Neural Network (NN), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Boosted Tree Regression (BTR) and Fine Tree Regression (FTR). NN and GPR is found to be the best performing model among all the used models with R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> equal to 99.868 % and 97.333 % respectively. Further, for these two best performed models, we predict the relation between the K and T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf> in both training and testing data. The relation between training and testing exhibits similar nature in the two models NN and GPR. This work guides a pathway for searching of materials for wide applications.

articleTitle: Analysing the Performance of Dense Net in the context of Tuberculosis Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease caused by the elusive Mycobacterium tuberculosis, leading to a persistent lung condition due to bacterial infection. The identification of tuberculosis (TB) is crucial, and chest X-ray images are routinely employed; nevertheless, manual interpretation is time-consuming and prone to errors. This research looked at; we introduced an advanced deep learning approach for classifying TB using chest X-rays. Our method involves leveraging deep learning algorithms to explore and identify optimal hypotheses for accurate predictions of TB. To address challenges like vanishing gradients and maximize feature reuse, we adopted the DenseNet architecture, well-known for its capabilities. This proposed model builds upon previous research, enhancing the accuracy of TB prediction using DenseNet, a powerful deep learning technique. The developed classifier, utilizing deep learning, achieved an impressive accuracy rate of 96%. This advancement holds promise for more efficient and reliable TB diagnosis through automated analysis of chest X-ray images.

articleTitle: Level Shifted PWM Technique for Minimum Component Switched Capacitor Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Nowadays, Multi-Level Inverters (MLIs) incorporating switched capacitors have become increasingly important for applications in both highvoltage AC scenarios and the renewable energy sector. The High Gain Switched Capacitor (HGSC) technique, designed to achieve the necessary output voltage magnitude, strategically utilizes a reduced number of DC sources based on capacitor voltage. Overcoming the challenge of designing a highly efficient, high-gain MLI with minimal sources and switches requires a comprehensive approach. The present study presents a new Nine-Level High Gain inverter topology that employs fewer capacitors, switches, and diodes compared to other HGSC-MLI configurations. The innovative inverter arrangement utilizes only one DC source, eight switches, and two capacitors to achieve Nine-Level output voltage waveforms. The Nine-Level High Gain inverter exhibits a remarkable ability to consistently generate high-quality voltage output under diverse conditions, employing modified PWM control techniques. The Phase Disposition Pulse width Modulation (PDPWM) technique is employed in this paper. Simulation studies have been meticulously conducted using MATLAB/Simulink, verifying the suggested nine-level inverter topology's efficiency.

articleTitle: Hysteresis Current Control Technique for Dual Output PFC Enabled Converters having the Unified Magnetics Stage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The following study presents an active Power Factor Correction (PFC) hysteresis current control technique for dual output AC-DC converters with a single magnetic component. By tracking a sinusoidal reference current input, which is computed based on the total output power required by the stages and the main AC voltage, control is accomplished. The control methodology used for the three converter topologies—Flyback, Pushpull, and Forward—is described in this work. Results of the simulation are displayed for the control operating at various input voltage operations and in all converters.

articleTitle: Lightweight Stereo Image Super-Resolution Using Parallax Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Over the past decade, advancements in cellular phone technology have drastically transformed mobile phones from mere communication devices into powerful mini-computers. The integration of high-quality cameras with smartphones has led to a surge in demand for high-resolution images captured using these compact handheld devices. Prevalent use of dual cameras in smartphones has further motivated the exploration of stereo image super-resolution (SSR) algorithms, which utilizes the complementary information provided by binocular system. In this paper, we propose a novel and simple SSR approach that incorporates depth-wise separable convolutions and a parallax attention module. The algorithm effectively employs depth-wise separable convolutions to extract features from both left and right view of stereo image pair. Additionally, the parallax attention module facilitates the integration of cross-view information to enhance the super-resolution process. By combining these techniques, the proposed SSR model, Light weight Parallax Attention Stereo Image Super-Resolution(L-PASSR) achieves a light weight design while still delivering comparable results in stereo image enhancement.

articleTitle: Design and Performance Validation of 3MW PV Grid connected Plant at VIT Chennai
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: As in recent times the energy consumption is increasing, and energy generation is stagnant. And conventional generation happens through fossil fuel, coal and water turbines. With these methods there are risks to the environmental impacts like CO2 production, pollution, adverse effects on climate. This research revolves around the design analysis of a 3MW system and performance analysis using PVSYST and HelioScope software at Standard test Conditions (STC). The initial site analysis is done using HelioScope and performance analysis and loss analysis using the PVSYST. This proposed system provides an inference to renewable energy and positive impact on the environment.

articleTitle: Analyzing Measured and De-Embedded S-Parameters of a Hybrid Network Unit for RF Characteristics of AlGaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The objective of this work is to measure and extract the S parameters of a hybrid network designed unit to analyze the RF characteristics of AlGaN HEMTs. The Noise Data tab plays a vital role in defining the characteristics of the Small Signal Noise Equivalent Circuit Model. In relative to frequency-dependent noise factors, the Noise Data tab can accomplish by an independent N-element vector aligned with different explicit frequency values. Additionally, to interpretation for frequency-dependent nonlinearity, the Nonlinearity Data tab empowers the input of a distinct characterization dependent calibration via data sourced from the RFDATA object. On working condition designed RF model unit of operational data is processed for different value of S-parameter. While the Operating Conditions Management entails and utilizing the Operating Conditions tab to define the simulation's circuit parameters. During the simulation process, data interpolation methods are utilized to accurately to represent the operating conditions of the Mean Square Power at -40 dBm within the frequency range of 1.9–2.3 GHz. Thereby enhancing the flexibility and assessment capabilities of AlGaN-based HEMTs for high frequency application device.

articleTitle: Automated People Counting System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Within the realm of computer vision, accurate people counting through video analysis is crucial, especially for crowd management and security applications. This paper introduces a system focused on automatically determining the count of individuals in both indoor and outdoor settings using a single camera and implementing it through Python-based OpenCV. The system extracts frames from video streams, establishes reference lines, detects individuals using the MobileNet-SSD object detection model, marks centroids on detected persons, tracks their movements, and determines the direction of movement to categorize entries or exits. Such technology is crucial not only for ensuring transportation safety but also for various businesses, especially smaller ones lacking extensive data for decision-making. The intelligent utilization of people counting data can significantly impact business operations beyond basic visitor statistics, shaping decisions and strategies effectively.

articleTitle: 9-Level Switched Capacitor Inverter with Level Shifted PWM Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: 9-level switched capacitor inverter (9-LSCI) is the goal of this work. The 9-LSCI is equipped with eight controlled switches, three capacitors, and a single DC source to generate nine output voltage levels for the inverter. The suggested inverter design allows the input voltage of the inverter to be raised to a 1:4 ratio. To further enhance the inverter output voltage quality, this study employs a level-shifted alternative phase opposition and disposition (APOD) PWM technique. The effectiveness of the 9-LSCI is assessed using a number of parameters, including as output voltage, peak voltage, harmonic distortion, and root mean square value (rms). Simulation studies using MATLAB/Simulink have been conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed inverter.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fetal Health Monitoring through TPOT and Optuna in Machine Learning-Driven Prenatal Care
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This study delves into the application of advanced machine learning techniques for the classification of fetal health, a critical domain in prenatal care. Utilizing a dataset based on cardiotocograms (CTGs), which record key fetal indicators like heart rate and uterine contractions, we compare two distinct machine learning approaches: a Random Forest Classifier optimized with the hyper parameter tuning tool Optuna, and a genetic programming-based model developed using TPOT (Tree-based Pipeline Optimization Tool).The Random Forest Classifier, configured with specific hyper parameters, delivered an accuracy of 94.13% and an impressive AUC of 0.9826. In contrast, the TPOT-optimized model, a Gradient Boosting Classifier with finely tuned parameters, achieved a higher accuracy of 96.01% and an internal CV score of approximately 95.24%. This comparison underscores the strengths and potential applications of these advanced methodologies in predicting and ensuring fetal health.

articleTitle: Design of Electric Vehicle Regenerative Braking System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Regenerative braking is an important technology in electric vehicles (EVs) that absorbs kinetic energy during deceleration or braking and transforms it back to electrical energy. This procedure is critical for increasing the efficiency and range of EVs. With rising market demand for electric vehicles, it is critical to improve their mechanisms to increase total capacity and advantages to the automotive sector. The expanding trends in this sector promote the use of techniques that improve driving efficiency. Regenerative braking, when combined with dual control techniques, can increase battery power management and reduce vehicle stopping time, saving fuel and energy. Advanced fuzzy logic control algorithms improve performance by tackling nonlinear elements like speed and braking torque, resulting in higher energy recovery. This review paper discusses improvements and approaches in regenerative braking systems, with a particular emphasis on dual control strategies. The goal is to assess the efficacy of dual control techniques for increasing braking performance and energy recovery. We provide a comprehensive literature analysis to emphasize the merits and limits of these tactics, comparing them to standard single control approaches. In addition, we will use a MATLAB model to show the practical consequences of dual control techniques in real-world EV applications. Our findings will highlight the importance of dual control techniques in developing regenerative braking systems, which improve both efficiency and driving dynamics in electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Analysis of Customer Churn for Telecom Company with SMOTE-ENN and Hyperparameter Tuning Randomized-SearchCV Technique in Advanced Machine Learning Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Customer churn analysis is an important task for telecom companies which aims to retain their customer base and enhance profitability. This paper proposes to help telecom companies predict the potential churn rate of their customers by using advanced machine learning technology. Specifically, this research intends to build a model with a Balanced Dataset and performance hyperparameter tuning using Randomized SearchCV. In this paper, the unbalance in the training set is subsequently addressed using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) with Edited Nearest Neighbor (ENN) and increases the performance of the model using Hyperparameter Tuning Randomized SearchCV. Following that, the effectiveness of advanced machine learning methods is compared by using "With Hyperparameter Tuning" and "Without Hyperparameter Tuning" techniques. Finally, this research focuses on providing valuable insights for telecom companies to proactively retain customers and enhance the overall satisfaction of customers.

articleTitle: Empowered Brain Tumor Detection Using Deep Learning Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: In medical diagnosis, early and accurate detection of brain tumors is crucial for effective treatment planning and improved patient outcomes. Traditional methods for brain tumor detection in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans and computed tomography (CT) scans can be time-consuming, subjective, and prone to human error. In this paper we overcome the problem in the domain of computer vision with deep learning approach. Deep learning models have emerged as a promising alternative, offering high accuracy and the potential for automation. This work investigates the application of the YOLOv8 deep learning model for real-time brain tumor detection in MRI scans. YOLOv8 offers a compelling balance between speed and accuracy, making it suitable for deployment in clinical settings. We evaluate the performance of YOLOv8 on a benchmark brain tumor dataset and compare it with other commonly used models. The results demonstrate that our YOLOv8 model achieves competitive accuracy (mentioning the specific metrics like accuracy, precision, recall) while maintaining real-time inference speed, paving the way for its potential use in real-time brain tumor detection during clinical examinations.

articleTitle: A Review of Vehicular Adhoc Network Routing and Congestion Control
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: In VANET, the efficiency of the RSUs positioned beside the roadways is crucial for both transportation and service provision. Direct communication between vehicles and infrastructure is supported by the network (V2V and V2I, correspondingly). The architecture of a VANET should satisfy several requirements to function properly and enable dependable real-time communication between vehicles while considering their low-power radio transmission of units, dynamic topology, and high mobility. Numerous routing protocols are suggested and assessed for VANETs. There are very few testbeds worldwide since they need a large count of wireless devices to test routing protocols with genuine VANETs and MANETs prototypes. By examining 25 publications, this survey aims to create a brief summary of VANET routing. In the current work, it offers an analysis of reliable routing models based on optimization algorithms. The best outcomes will be displayed once the performance metrics of the works that were examined are examined.

articleTitle: Exploring the Efficacy of Federated-Continual Learning Nodes with Attention-Based Classifier for Robust Web Phishing Detection: An Empirical Investigation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Web phishing poses a dynamic threat, requiring detection systems to quickly adapt to the latest tactics. Traditional approaches of accumulating data and periodically retraining models are outpaced. We propose a novel paradigm combining federated learning and continual learning, enabling distributed nodes to continually update models on streams of new phishing data, without accumulating data. These locally adapted models are then aggregated at a central server via federated learning. To enhance detection, we introduce a custom attention-based classifier model with residual connections, tailored for web phishing, leveraging attention mechanisms to capture intricate phishing patterns. We evaluate our hybrid learning paradigm across continual learning strategies (cumulative, replay, MIR, LwF) and model architectures through an empirical investigation. Our main contributions are: (1) a new hybrid federated-continual learning paradigm for robust web phishing detection, and (2) a novel attention + residual connections based model explicitly designed for this task, attaining 0.93 accuracy, 0.90 precision, 0.96 recall and 0.93 f1-score with the LwF strategy, outperforming traditional approaches in detecting emerging phishing threats while retaining past knowledge.

articleTitle: Optimizing Cloud Computing Energy Efficiency with a Grasshopper-Inspired Technique for Virtual Machine Migration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This research paper presents a novel approach using the grasshopper algorithm to improve the energy efficiency of virtual machine (VM) migration in cloud computing. This methodology reframes resource allocation techniques to address the complexity of VM selection from heavily utilized physical machines (PMs). Its effectiveness is evaluated in comparison to traditional VM migration techniques and optimization algorithms such as Firefly and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). Significant metrics that act as evaluation criteria for algorithm include the reduction of energy usage, mitigation of service level agreement violations (SLA-V), and overall resource optimization. The research paper not only presents a novel approach but also provides significant perspectives for the advancement of dynamic resource allocation in cloud systems in the future. It creates opportunities for enhancing energy efficiency in the constantly changing field of cloud computing by exploring computational approaches inspired by nature.

articleTitle: EmoSpeak: An Emotionally Intelligent Text-to-Speech System for Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The paper delves into the obstacles confronting individuals with visual impairments, especially those experiencing blurred vision due to medical conditions or aging, when navigating technology, notably chat services. People with weak eyesight face issues such as inaccessible user interfaces, challenges in reading and inputting text, interpreting visual cues, and engaging in real-time interactions. The central aim is to propose a chat application specifically tailored to enhance communication for this demographic. The proposed solution integrates cutting-edge Speech-To-Text (STT) and Text-To-Speech (TTS) conversion, alongside emotion detection using Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM technology). This holistic approach seeks to create a more accessible and inclusive digital communication platform, thereby empowering users to better understand and express their emotions in online interactions.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches for Waste Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Waste management is a global problem that requires different solutions from country to country as there is no standardized approach. However, efficient waste recycling offers significant opportunities for government revenue generation. Accordingly, our research proposes an automated technology that can accurately detect and sort waste. Recognizing the key role of waste sorting in cost-effective recycling, the goal of our research was to identify and sort individual waste items shown in photographs. Using deep learning techniques, including convolutional neural networks such as ResNet, MobileNetV2 and DenseNet, our goal is to optimize waste management processes.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Fitness Function in Genetic Algorithm for Fetal Brain MRI Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Medical image classification plays a vital role in aiding diagnosis and treatment planning. Fetal magnetic resonance imaging has appeared as a crucial diagnostic tool for prenatal evaluation, providing detailed insights into fetal development and potential abnormalities. This paper shows a comparative evaluation of various fitness functions in genetic algorithm for fetal MRI image classification. The fitness function is a pivotal component in genetic algorithms, playing a crucial role in guiding the evolutionary process towards optimal solutions. The proposed study utilizes accuracy, precision, recall, f1- score, specificity and cross- entropy loss as a fitness function in genetic algorithms for fetal MR image classification. The classification results are evaluated using various performance metrics. The simulation outcomes show the effectiveness of the genetic algorithm framework in accurately classifying fetal MR images. Furthermore, the analysis reveals insights into the impact of different fitness functions on the classification performance, providing valuable guidance for optimizing the algorithm for fetal MR image classification tasks. This research contributes to the advancement of medical image analysis techniques and has implications for improving prenatal diagnosis and patient care.

articleTitle: Detection of Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) Severity from Fundus Photographs using Conv-ViT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant rise in the global prevalence of diabetes, affecting individuals across all age groups. Among those with longstanding diabetes, a common complication known as Diabetic Retinopathy (DR) poses a substantial risk, leading to vision impairment. DR stands as a major concern due to its widespread impact on individuals with diabetes worldwide. Traditionally, the assessment of DR severity has relied on manual evaluation by ophthalmologists using Fundus photography-based retina images, a process prone to time constraints and inconsistency. This paper proposes an automated approach for categorizing the severity stages of DR, aiming to alleviate the limitations of manual diagnosis. Our methodology employs a hybrid feature extraction technique, integrating Convolutional and Vision Transformer models, to infer the severity of DR from fundus photographs. The experiments are conducted using the publicly available APTOS-2019 blindness detection dataset, facilitating comprehensive evaluation and validation of our proposed method.

articleTitle: A Rescue Aid for Hazardous Situations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: A human rescue aid robot is a type of robot designed to assist in rescue and emergency situations where human lives may be at risk. Disasters such as earthquakes, storms, floods, fires, wars, bombings, and terrorist attacks cause considerable property damage and loss of life. Timely support can save many lives, but human entry into these dangerous areas is risky. Compact aerial vehicles can navigate debris, gathering and transmitting data to ground control stations. Data should be displayed on a user-friendly interface and the bot should be controllable via hand gestures, joysticks, or other methods. These compact, agile bots, equipped with cameras, microphones, thermal sensors, and manipulators, improve rescue operations while reducing human risk. The proposed system features a wireless, long-range bot with low communication latency, capable of recording temperature, humidity, and air quality. Data is transmitted to a ground station via an I2C bus with varying frequencies. A Human Machine Interface (HMI) is used to control and receive information from the bot. The proposed human rescue assistance robots have the potential to greatly improve the effectiveness and speed of rescue operations, enabling responders to find and assist those in need as soon as possible while lowering the risk to human life.

articleTitle: Multi Disease Detection And Diagnosis Through Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Health Cure is a groundbreaking medical initiative aimed at revolutionizing early disease detection through the integration of advanced medical technology and sophisticated algorithms. This paper focuses on identifying and evaluating seven critical diseases, including COVID-19, brain tumors, breast cancer, diabetes, Alzheimer’s, pneumonia, and heart disease. The complexity of disease mechanisms and diverse symptoms poses a significant challenge in creating effective early diagnosis tools and efficient treatment plans on a global scale. This work leverages a variety of techniques, such as Random Forest, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and XG Boost, to address the unmet need for accurate and timely disease diagnosis. Traditional diagnosis based on symptoms proves challenging for medical professionals to make the reliable detection of diseases a formidable task. To overcome these challenges, machine learning (ML) and deep learning algorithms plays a pivotal role in predicting and detecting high-risk diseases. The integration of supervised ML algorithms and deep learning techniques demonstrates substantial potential in outperforming existing disease diagnosis systems. After the prediction we design a user interface for users to get the test results immediately in our home just a few clicks. In this work, detect and predict seven diseases in one platform or multiple diseases under one platform using ML and DL techniques. And provide a user interface for users to get a test results immediately in our home just a few clicks after that provide a food, medicine and doctor recommendations. And our novel idea is detect heart beat rate by using heart beat sensor(MAX30100) for monitoring real time heart beat sensing in heart disease UI page, By supplying pertinent symptoms, machine learning is utilized in disease inference systems to forecast human illnesses. This paper presents a comprehensive platform capable of detecting and predicting multiple diseases using ML and DL methods.

articleTitle: GAN-based Image Inpainting Techniques: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Image inpainting is the process of completing or reconstructing areas in an image that are absent or damaged using information extracted from the surrounding parts of the same image. The output inpainted images should be realistic and challenging to discern from the original images. Image degradation can occur due to various factors, posing a significant challenge for image inpainting, which makes it a vital and intricate task in the domain of image processing. This paper centers around a variety of image inpainting techniques that rely on Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), which have gained prominence lately. The paper further discusses various datasets available for image inpainting. An overview of commonly used evaluation metrics is provided, and the performance of various GAN-based image inpainting methods in terms of these evaluation metrics is discussed.

articleTitle: Quantitative Analysis and Optimization of Sensor Deployment for Enhanced Activity Recognition in Smart Home Environments: A Multidimensional Approach to Data-Driven Intelligence and Efficiency in Universal Computing Spaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the enhancement of smart home automation and monitoring systems through the application of advanced activity recognition algorithms and sensor deployment optimization. We start by taking a CASAS dataset capturing a wide range of daily living activities, detected through an array of environmental sensors. This study conducts an in-depth analysis of activity recognition performance, leveraging precision, recall, and f1score metrics to identify areas for improvement in existing machine learning models. Further, we investigate sensor activation data to propose optimizations in sensor deployment, aimed at increasing the accuracy of activity recognition while reducing unnecessary sensor data processing. Through temporal analysis of activity patterns, we develop predictive models that forecast future activities with significant accuracy, facilitating smarter resource management and personalized automation strategies. This paper also explores the implications of our findings on user experience enhancement. Our methodology showcases the integration of machine learning techniques, statistical analysis, and practical considerations for deploying smart home technologies. The results indicate a promising avenue for future research and development in smart environments, with potential applications extending beyond residential settings to include healthcare facilities and office spaces. The findings underscore the importance of adaptive and intelligent systems in enhancing the quality of life through technology.

articleTitle: Real-World Evaluation: Hybrid Recommender System and User Engagement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Recommender systems are essential for social media platforms, personalizing content suggestions, and driving user engagement. This study investigates the impact of a hybrid recommender system on user behavior within a real-world social media platform. The system combines content-based filtering and collaborative filtering techniques to deliver personalized recommendations to users. User engagement is evaluated over six months using various metrics beyond clicks, including likes, plays, stream time, comments, shares, and returning users. Analysis revealed significant improvements in user engagement following system implementation. Users displayed a 12.815% increase in likes, indicating heightened interest in recommended content. Plays surged by 124.159%, suggesting a solid alignment between recommendations and user preferences. Stream time also saw a substantial rise of 117.349%, further highlighting deeper user engagement with the recommended content. Positive trends were also observed in engagement depth, with increases of 5.589% in comments and 59.825% in shares, signifying user satisfaction and a willingness to interact with and share the discovered content. Notably, the number of returning users witnessed a remarkable growth of 287.704%, demonstrating the system's effectiveness in fostering user retention. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of hybrid recommender systems and their potential to enhance user experience in social media environments. The study highlights how these systems can personalize content discovery, increase user satisfaction, and ultimately strengthen platform loyalty.

articleTitle: Handling Missing Data in Graph Networks with Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: With recent advancements in social networks and knowledge graphs, graph data has become more popular and the use of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) in graph analysis tasks has been a great success. GCN model assumes all features of all nodes are available and it works by smoothening node features. But, due to privacy-protection policies, copyright restrictions, and sensor malfunctioning during data collection, real-world graphs suffer from incompleteness and missing features. Conventional methods could only produce inconsistent and unstable results, the main reason for which is, that feature imputation and graph learning are unrelated. To address this gap there are network models that are capable of imputing node feature information and learning the graph within the same architecture. GCN with missing features (GCN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MF</inf>) is a modified GCN model that outperformed conventional methods for node classification. The proposed method utilizes the capabilities of GCN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MF</inf> while producing a better estimate of missing features. This is achieved by performing an unsupervised clustering of the graph data using K-means and applying GCN<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">MF</inf> for each cluster. Feature matrix from each cluster is then combined and passed through a GCN model. Experiments conducted over the model with two popular graph datasets for node classification tasks produced a better accuracy score

articleTitle: Suggestion Mining for Mobile APP Quality Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: User feedback is essential for mobile apps to continuously improve. However, obtaining insightful suggestions from user reviews still poses a major challenge. In order to address this issue, this study suggests a brand-new rule-based method for suggestion mining that focuses on the action verbs’ capacity to provide information. To detect user evaluations with suggestions, our approach makes use of verb semantics and pre-established criteria based on action verbs. We undertake a comprehensive performance evaluation on an actual dataset of mobile app evaluations to determine its efficacy. The outcomes demonstrate the substantial potential of our rule-based methodology, attaining superior memory and precision in identifying suggestions in reviews. Through the utilization of action verbs’ rich information, our approach provides a useful and effective way to automatically derive actionable suggestions from user reviews. We obtained above 89% accuracy for enhanced proposed method. In the end, this helps to improve the quality of mobile apps by enabling data-driven adjustments based on user reviews.

articleTitle: A Bird Eye View on Next Generation Smart Farming Based on IoT with Machine Learning Approach – A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Agriculture in India is vital to the economy, employing a large section of the population and boosting GDP. Despite its historical importance, the industry faces several problems, including declining production and monsoon unpredictability. This research work presents a review of the role of new technologies, notably IoT and drone technology, in tackling these difficulties and promoting sustainable agriculture in India. The study starts by explaining agriculture's role in India's economy and society using historical and statistical data. It demonstrates the recent decline in agricultural production and the need for new ideas to revive the industry. Based on this, the article investigates how IoT devices and drones could transform agricultural operations. It shows how field-deployed IoT sensors can monitor temperature, humidity, and soil moisture in real time via thorough explanations and examples. It also examines how drones with multispectral and thermal sensors might help farmers identify crop illnesses and stress factors early and take immediate action. The report discusses connectivity, data security, and cost-effectiveness when utilizing IoT and drone technologies in agriculture. The report highlights the need for stakeholder collaboration to overcome these challenges and successfully integrate technology into agricultural practices.

Author Keywords: Internet of things (IoT)and DHT11 Sensor etc

articleTitle: P&O MPPT-based Wind Power Generation Scheme for Telecom Tower Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: This novel proposes a hybrid power generation system to solve telecommunication industry issues, such as increased operational expenditures (OPEX) and carbon emissions from grid and diesel generator (DG) dependence. This hybrid system uses a wind energy conversion system (WECS) as its main power source for base transceiver stations (BTS), along with a secondary battery backup. This particular setup utilizes a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) with a diode bridge rectifier which is known for its dependability and affordability. To extract the maximum power from the wind energy conversion system even at varying wind speeds and ensure realistic implementation, maximum power point tracking (MPPT) operation using the perturb and observe (P&O) algorithm is employed with the proportional-integral (PI) controller. Its reliable performance against disturbances from both the source and load fluctuations, and its ease of design and implementation, make this control system noteworthy. The MATLAB/Simulink environment is used to run extensive simulations to evaluate the proposed scheme for powering telecom towers through a PMSG-based system.

articleTitle: Real-Time Population Tracking & Personal Information Log with Image Processing: Haar Cascade & LBPH Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: In order to know whether a person is attending a class, meeting, or an assigned task, attendance is taken which is recorded for future clarification. In spite of the traditional method of addressing each person, here we propose the use of cameras with methodologies like Haar cascade and LBPH (Local Binary Patterns Histograms). In this proposal, the user is able to note the attendance of a group of people simultaneously. The faces detected and recognized using these methods are stored in a file. The entire setup can be built using Raspberry Pi, a camera module, and an SD card for storing the data. The setup demonstrates an accuracy of 96 percent during testing.

articleTitle: A Review of Attention Based Model for Sentimental Analysis using NLP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Attention mechanisms are an important part of deep learning models that help in handling sequential data. They provide a flexible and effective way to deal with sequential data by focusing on relevant information. This mechanism is widely used in various deep learning architectures and is essential in natural language processing tasks like sentiment analysis. Attention mechanisms address the problem of traditional sequence-to-sequence models. The purpose of this paper is to provide an overview of the latest attention mechanisms in sentiment analysis and to analyze various models for attention in natural language processing. This work investigates the performance of various attention network models and analyzes their accuracy in sentiment polarity detection. Additionally, the paper examines diverse datasets used in sentiment analysis, highlights research gaps, and outlines potential future directions in the research area.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Stand-alone and Hybrid Multi-UAV Network Architectures for Disaster Response Missions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Disaster response missions demand robust and efficient communication networks to coordinate unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) effectively. The choice of network architecture in UAV networks is application-specific and depends on factors such as scalability, fault tolerance, and the level of autonomy. This paper presents a comprehensive comparative analysis of different network architectures—both stand-alone and hybrid—in the context of disaster missions. The advantages and challenges of each architecture are studied and performance is evaluated concerning factors crucial to disaster response, including resource efficiency, latency, communication overhead, scalability, and adaptability. The findings provide valuable insights into the suitability of each architecture in disaster response contexts, facilitating informed decision-making in designing resilient UAV communication networks for critical missions.

articleTitle: Smart Healthcare Systems: A Survey of IoT and AI Technologies for Heart Disease Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The surge in heart-related issues is linked to lifestyle changes and increased fast food consumption. The convergence of cloud computing, IoT and machine learning for the prediction of cardio vascular disease is examined in this survey. In order to combat the worldwide increase in Cardio Vascular Disease, researchers are investigating novel strategies that make use of IoT sensors, ensemble approaches and machine learning for ongoing health monitoring. By combining these technologies, the IoT-ML-Cloud paradigm seeks to improve the accuracy of Cardio Vascular Disease prediction. It also emphasizes the importance of cloud computing and data mining for large-scale medical data analysis, as well as key findings from various ML algorithms in Cardio Vascular Disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Review on a Smart Solar-Powered Greenhouse System using IoT Sensors for Automated Internal Climate Control and Crop Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: Intelligent technology integration into farming practices is a revolutionary development with possibilities for increased production and sustainability. This thorough investigation involves the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) sensors in solar-powered greenhouse systems to facilitate advanced crop surveillance and inner climate control. The synthesis explores the interplay between solar energy and IoT advancements, drawing on reliable sources to elaborate on the advantages and challenges of this innovative farming strategy. This study explores how renewable energy, particularly solar power, may be integrated into greenhouse architecture. It also covers the technical details of installing solar panels, energy storage, and how they work with other energy sources. This article explores how IoT sensors might improve crop surveillance and streamline inner climate control. The final section highlights the emerging trends, navigates through potential obstacles, and highlights the critical importance of intelligent solar-powered greenhouses moving towards the path to sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: Cognitive Detection of Anomalies in Autonomous In-Vehicle Network Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Advancements in Power, Communication and Intelligent Systems (APCI)
abstract: The research addresses the critical issue of detecting anomalies in autonomous in-vehicle network communication, focusing on the vulnerability of infotainment systems to denial-of-service attacks. The aim is to explore and compare traditional Machine Learning (ML) and advanced Deep Learning (DL) models for the detection of DoS attacks within Controller Area Network (CAN) communications. By evaluating the performance of various ML and DL algorithms, including Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, RandomForest, Feed Forward Neural Networks, and LSTM architectures, the study aims to enhance intrusion detection capabilities in vehicular communication systems. The significance of the research lies in identifying the advantages of DL methods in capturing complex patterns and temporal dependencies within the CAN network, thus contributing to fortifying the security of automotive networks against evolving threats. The results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed models in detecting and mitigating DoS attacks, with DL methods showing promise in automatic learning and adaptability to intricate network structures. This study provides valuable insights for future research endeavors aimed at enhancing the cybersecurity of autonomous vehicles.
